sequences.description: Brokered-flow attack: configure an OIDC IdP, then mutate the IdP config to point to an attacker-controlled JWKS (trust anchor substitution) and attempt re-auth. The broker must not accept tokens whose semantic issuer/audience are not bound to the intended trust anchor.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Brokered OIDC flow succeeded after trust-anchor substitution (attacker JWKS), implying the broker consumed identity claims without enforcing verification against the intended issuer/key policy.

sequences.description: I5: Token exchange must enforce subject_token audience binding. Obtain a token for client-A, then attempt token exchange at client-B requesting audience=client-B. Expected: exchange rejected (or at least not mint a token usable as client-B) because subject_token was not intended for client-B.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions of an exchanged token must not exceed the upstream intent of the subject_token; token exchange must validate that the subject_token is acceptable for the requested audience.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange succeeded even though subject_token was minted for a different client/audience; broker may be ignoring subject_token audience binding, enabling permission escalation to client-B.
